findings.title: Hardcoded AWS Access Key ID
findings.explanation: Recognizable AWS Access Key ID committed to source. Committed credentials allow persistent unauthorized cloud resource access. Move credentials to environment variables.
findings.evidence:
1 | // SEC-001: Synthetic AWS-shaped value; this is not a credential.
> 2 | const awsAccessKey = "AKIA****************";
  3 | 
  4 | // SEC-002: Illustrates unsafe SQL construction; do not execute this sample.

findings.title: Command Injection via Dynamic Shell Execution
findings.explanation: Shell command constructed with dynamic variables passed to exec(). An attacker can append shell operators (; | &&) to execute arbitrary commands. Use execFile() or spawn() with explicit argument arrays.
findings.evidence:
6 | 
  7 | // SEC-003: Harmless fixed command text, included only as inert scanner input.
> 8 | exec(`echo ${userInput}`);
  9 | 
  10 | // SEC-004: Empty catch example, included only as inert scanner input.

findings.title: Potential SQL Injection (Dynamic Query Concatenation)
findings.explanation: Raw SQL query constructed via dynamic string concatenation or template literal. This pattern can allow attackers to manipulate query logic or extract data. Use parameterized queries ($1, ? or prepared statements).
findings.evidence:
3 | 
  4 | // SEC-002: Illustrates unsafe SQL construction; do not execute this sample.
> 5 | const query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + userId;
  6 | 
  7 | // SEC-003: Harmless fixed command text, included only as inert scanner input.

findings.title: Empty Catch Block (Suppressed Exceptions)
findings.explanation: An empty catch block silently swallows runtime errors, concealing underlying bugs, failed I/O, or broken security assumptions. Log the exception or handle it explicitly.
